title: Vesuvius Challenge: First Complete Herculaneum Scroll (PHerc. 1667) Virtually Unwrapped & Read End-to-End
aiSystem: Vesuvius Challenge 3D U-Net & Self-Supervised 3D DINO Ink Models
whyItMatters: Sealed since Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD, the entire surviving Herculaneum scroll PHerc. 1667 was non-destructively unrolled and read end-to-end using 3D CT deep learning—recovering a lost Stoic ethics treatise.
summary: On June 25, 2026, the open-source Vesuvius Challenge (led by Brent Seales, Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, ESRF, and global ML contributors) achieved a historic milestone in computational archaeology: virtually unwrapping and reading the entire surviving portion of carbonized Herculaneum scroll PHerc. 1667 end-to-end without physically opening it—the first complete ancient bookroll recovered since the 79 AD eruption of Mount Vesuvius. Using synchrotron X-ray micro-CT scans paired with open-source 3D segmentation and ink-detection neural networks (3D U-Nets and self-supervised 3D DINO transfer models), papyrologists identified PHerc. 1667 as a previously unknown 2nd-century BC Stoic ethics treatise naming Aristocreon, while parallel scans recovered Philodemus’s On Gods Book 8 (PHerc. 139) and broke open first Greek letters in PHerc. 306B and PHerc. 211 in November 2026.
technicalHighlights: First complete non-destructive virtual unwrapping and end-to-end reading of a carbonized Herculaneum papyrus scroll (PHerc. 1667) buried since 79 AD.
Recovered previously unknown classical antiquity texts including a 2nd-century BC Stoic ethics treatise naming Aristocreon and Philodemus’s On Gods, Book 8 (PHerc. 139).
Open-source 3D U-Net + self-supervised 3D DINO transfer pipelines generalized zero-shot to unlock additional unread scrolls (PHerc. 306B and PHerc. 211) in November 2026.
caveats: Individual faint letter readings rely on learned ink-probability reconstructions verified by the Vesuvius papyrology team; formal critical editions of the full recovered texts are in preparation.

scoreRationale.foundational: Solves a 2,000-year-old physical barrier by recovering complete lost works of ancient Greek philosophy from carbonized scrolls without destroying them.
scoreRationale.ripple: Unlocks hundreds of remaining unread Herculaneum scrolls and establishes a general 3D CT + deep-learning paradigm for damaged historical artifacts.
scoreRationale.verification: Independently corroborated by synchrotron imaging, open-source reproducible ML weights/code, and classical papyrology teams.
scoreRationale.velocity: Progressed from first isolated letters in late 2023 to reading an entire scroll end-to-end and scaling across multiple new scrolls by 2026.
